package cli

import (
 "bytes"
 "encoding/json"
 "os"
 "path/filepath"
 "strings"
 "testing"

 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/gitdir"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMetadataCompleteOperationTrace(t *testing.T) {
 testutil.IsolateGitConfigEnv(t)
 repoRoot := setupTestRepo(t)
 writeSettings(t, testSettingsEnabled)
 writeClaudeHooksFixture(t)
 repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(repoRoot)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 defer repo.Close()
 message := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
 require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(message, []byte("trace commit\n"), 0o600))
 for _, tc := range []struct{
  name string
  operation func(t *testing.T)
 }{
  {"session-cwd", func(t *testing.T) { store, err := session.NewStateStore(t.Context()); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, store) }},
  {"session-explicit", func(t *testing.T) { store, err := session.NewStateStoreForWorktree(t.Context(), repoRoot); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, store) }},
  {"checkpoint-queue", func(t *testing.T) { queue, err := checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo(t.Context(), repo); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, queue) }},
  {"prepare-commit", func(t *testing.T) { s := &strategy.ManualCommitStrategy{}; require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(t.Context(), message, "")); content, err := os.ReadFile(message); require.NoError(t, err); require.Equal(t, "trace commit\n", string(content)) }},
  {"status", func(t *testing.T) { var output bytes.Buffer; require.NoError(t, runStatus(t.Context(), &output, false, false)); require.Contains(t, output.String(), "Enabled") }},
  {"codex-discovery", func(t *testing.T) { discovery := codex.ResolveHookDiscovery(t.Context()); require.Equal(t, codex.HookDiscoveryResolved, discovery.State); require.NoError(t, discovery.Diagnostic); require.Equal(t, filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".codex", "hooks.json"), discovery.DiscoveredHooks.Path()) }},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
   gitdir.Reset()
   t.Cleanup(paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache)
   t.Cleanup(gitdir.Reset)
   tracePath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "trace.jsonl")
   t.Setenv("GIT_TRACE2_EVENT", tracePath)
   tc.operation(t)
   commands := metadataOperationCommands(t, tracePath)
   t.Logf("complete operation: %d Git subprocesses; argv=%q", len(commands), commands)
   testutil.RunGit(t, repoRoot, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
   require.Len(t, metadataOperationCommands(t, tracePath), len(commands)+1, "positive control must add a real Git start event")
  })
 }
}

func metadataOperationCommands(t *testing.T, tracePath string) [][]string {
 t.Helper()
 data, err := os.ReadFile(tracePath)
 if os.IsNotExist(err) { return nil }
 require.NoError(t, err)
 var commands [][]string
 for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.TrimSpace(string(data)), "\n") {
  var event struct { Event string `json:"event"`; Argv []string `json:"argv"` }
  require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &event))
  if event.Event == "start" { commands = append(commands, event.Argv) }
 }
 return commands
}
EOF

tail -5 /tmp/split5-base-check.log",max_output_tokens:1200}));

 writeClaudeHooksFixture(t)
 repo, err := gitrepo.OpenPath(repoRoot)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 defer repo.Close()
 message := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
 require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(message, []byte("trace commit\n"), 0o600))
 for _, tc := range []struct{
  name string
  operation func(t *testing.T)
 }{
  {"session-cwd", func(t *testing.T) { store, err := session.NewStateStore(t.Context()); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, store) }},
  {"session-explicit", func(t *testing.T) { store, err := session.NewStateStoreForWorktree(t.Context(), repoRoot); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, store) }},
  {"checkpoint-queue", func(t *testing.T) { queue, err := checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo(t.Context(), repo); require.NoError(t, err); require.NotNil(t, queue) }},
  {"prepare-commit", func(t *testing.T) { s := &strategy.ManualCommitStrategy{}; require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(t.Context(), message, "")); content, err := os.ReadFile(message); require.NoError(t, err); require.Equal(t, "trace commit\n", string(content)) }},
  {"status", func(t *testing.T) { var output bytes.Buffer; require.NoError(t, runStatus(t.Context(), &output, false, false)); require.Contains(t, output.String(), "Enabled") }},
  {"codex-discovery", func(t *testing.T) { discovery := codex.ResolveHookDiscovery(t.Context()); require.Equal(t, codex.HookDiscoveryResolved, discovery.State); require.NoError(t, discovery.Diagnostic); require.Equal(t, filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".codex", "hooks.json"), discovery.DiscoveredHooks.Path()) }},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
   gitdir.Reset()
   t.Cleanup(paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache)
   t.Cleanup(gitdir.Reset)
   tracePath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "trace.jsonl")

   require.Len(t, metadataOperationCommands(t, tracePath), len(commands)+1, "positive control must add a real Git start event")
  })
 }
}

func metadataOperationCommands(t *testing.T, tracePath string) [][]string {
 t.Helper()
 data, err := os.ReadFile(tracePath)
 if os.IsNotExist(err) { return nil }
 require.NoError(t, err)
 var commands [][]string
 for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.TrimSpace(string(data)), "\n") {
  var event struct { Event string `json:"event"`; Argv []string `json:"argv"` }
  require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &event))
  if event.Event == "start" { commands = append(commands, event.Argv) }
 }
 return commands
}

package cli

import (
 "bytes"
 "os"
 "path/filepath"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex"
 "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"

 "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

type metadataConsumerLayout struct {
 root, gitDir, commonDir, id string
}

func TestMetadataConsumersAgreeAcrossGitLayouts(t *testing.T) {
 // The consumers discover from CWD; each case owns the process-wide discovery state.
 testutil.IsolateGitConfigEnv(t)
 for _, layout := range []string{"ordinary", "linked", "dot-bare", "bare-storage", "separate", "submodule", "linked-submodule", "submodule-in-linked-superproject", "relative-pointer", "moved-registration", "alias"} {
  t.Run(layout, func(t *testing.T) {
   fixture := newMetadataConsumerLayout(t, layout)
   t.Chdir(fixture.root)
   paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
   t.Cleanup(paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache)
   metadata, err := gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata(fixture.root)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   require.Equal(t, fixture.id, metadata.WorktreeID)

func newMetadataConsumerLayout(t *testing.T, layout string) metadataConsumerLayout {
 t.Helper()
 tmp := t.TempDir()
 main := filepath.Join(tmp, "main")
 testutil.InitRepo(t, main)
 testutil.WriteFile(t, main, "initial.txt", "initial\n")
 testutil.GitAdd(t, main, "initial.txt")
 testutil.GitCommit(t, main, "initial")
 f := metadataConsumerLayout{root: main, gitDir: filepath.Join(main, ".git"), commonDir: filepath.Join(main, ".git")}
 switch layout {
 case "ordinary": return f
 case "separate":
  storage := filepath.Join(tmp, "storage")
  testutil.RunGit(t, main, "init", "--separate-git-dir", storage)
  return metadataConsumerLayout{root: main, gitDir: storage, commonDir: storage}
 case "dot-bare", "bare-storage":
  name := "storage"
  if layout == "dot-bare" { name = ".bare" }
  storage := filepath.Join(tmp, name)
  testutil.RunGit(t, tmp, "clone", "--bare", main, storage)
  linked := filepath.Join(tmp, "linked")
  testutil.RunGit(t, tmp, "--git-dir", storage, "worktree", "add", "-b", "linked", linked)
  return metadataConsumerLayout{root: linked, gitDir: filepath.Join(storage, "worktrees", "linked"), commonDir: storage, id: "linked"}
 case "submodule", "linked-submodule", "submodule-in-linked-superproject":
  source := filepath.Join(tmp, "source")
  testutil.InitRepo(t, source)
  testutil.WriteFile(t, source, "module.txt", "module\n")
  testutil.GitAdd(t, source, "module.txt")
  testutil.GitCommit(t, source, "module")
  testutil.RunGit(t, main, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "submodule", "add", source, "module")
  testutil.GitAdd(t, main, ".")
  testutil.GitCommit(t, main, "add module")
  module := filepath.Join(main, "module")
  storage := filepath.Join(main, ".git", "modules", "module")
  if layout == "linked-submodule" {
   linked := filepath.Join(tmp, "module-linked")
   testutil.RunGit(t, module, "worktree", "add", "-b", "module-linked", linked)
   return metadataConsumerLayout{root: linked, gitDir: filepath.Join(storage, "worktrees", "module-linked"), commonDir: storage, id: "module-linked"}
  }
  if layout == "submodule-in-linked-superproject" {
   super := filepath.Join(tmp, "super-linked")
   testutil.RunGit(t, main, "worktree", "add", "-b", "super-linked", super)
   testutil.RunGit(t, super, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "submodule", "update", "--init")
   module = filepath.Join(super, "module")
   storage = filepath.Join(main, ".git", "worktrees", "super-linked", "modules", "module")
  }
  return metadataConsumerLayout{root: module, gitDir: storage, commonDir: storage}
 }
 linked := filepath.Join(tmp, "linked")
 testutil.RunGit(t, main, "worktree", "add", "-b", "linked", linked)
 f.root, f.gitDir, f.id = linked, filepath.Join(main, ".git", "worktrees", "linked"), "linked"
 switch layout {
 case "relative-pointer":
  rel, err := filepath.Rel(linked, f.gitDir)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(linked, ".git"), []byte("gitdir: "+rel+"\n"), 0o600))
 case "moved-registration":
  moved := filepath.Join(tmp, "moved")
  testutil.RunGit(t, main, "worktree", "move", linked, moved)
  f.root = moved
 case "alias":
  alias := filepath.Join(tmp, "alias")
  require.NoError(t, os.Symlink(main, alias))
  f.gitDir, f.commonDir = filepath.Join(alias, ".git", "worktrees", "linked"), filepath.Join(alias, ".git")
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(linked, ".git"), []byte("gitdir: "+f.gitDir+"\n"), 0o600))
 }
 return f
}

# Edge-case matrix

Walk the categories the change touches. These are ordinary states, not exotic ones -- every row
below appeared as a real review finding or a real bug.

## Git and paths

- [ ] Normal checkout
- [ ] Conventional linked worktree
- [ ] `.bare/worktrees` layout
- [ ] Separate Git directory
- [ ] Ordinary submodule
- [ ] Linked submodule
- [ ] Symlinked checkout or directory
- [ ] Symlinked final file, and dangling symlink
- [ ] Missing, unreadable, malformed, and non-regular paths
- [ ] Path containment still holds *after* symlink resolution
- [ ] No remote, fork remote, raw URL, multiple push URLs, elected remote

## State and persistence

- [ ] Absent
- [ ] User-owned but not managed by this tool
- [ ] Partial
- [ ] Current
- [ ] Outdated
- [ ] Invalid
- [ ] Unreadable
- [ ] Unresolved
- [ ] Unsupported
- [ ] Older persisted format
- [ ] Unknown fields preserved on rewrite
- [ ] Nil versus empty serialized values (`null` versus `[]`)

## Process and concurrency

- [ ] Cancellation before the durable write
- [ ] Cancellation during each state that holds an external resource or prepared transaction
- [ ] Cancellation after the write but before state save
- [ ] Graceful abort releases locks, temporary files, pipes, goroutines, and child processes
- [ ] The next real operation succeeds immediately after cancellation or failure
- [ ] Lock contention and lock timeout
- [ ] Safety, liveness, and fairness evaluated separately
- [ ] Deadline-bearing, cancelable-without-deadline, and non-cancelable callers retain their contract
- [ ] Shared blocking, polling, or retry changes audited across all caller classes
- [ ] Concurrent writer from another process (the real one, not an in-process stand-in)
- [ ] Cleanup that removes state a later step needs
- [ ] Retry after a partial operation
- [ ] Idempotent rerun

## Environment and user interaction

- [ ] Variable unset
- [ ] Variable present but empty
- [ ] Tool-specific inherited variables cannot override the explicitly selected target
- [ ] Ambient variables poisoned in tests to prove repository, config, and credential isolation
- [ ] No TTY
- [ ] Raw-mode TTY
- [ ] `NO_COLOR` or non-styled output
- [ ] Windows and missing POSIX shell
- [ ] Expired, missing, and explicitly selected login contexts

## Failure semantics

- [ ] Typed sentinel errors matched with `errors.Is`, never by string
- [ ] Presence distinguished from a non-empty value (`os.LookupEnv`)
- [ ] Caller cancellation propagated separately from a child timeout
- [ ] Process exit success distinguished from domain-operation success
- [ ] Protocol response, process result, and local cancellation state agree
- [ ] Internal timeout or contention traced to the outermost command, hook, request, or job result
- [ ] Contention or temporary unavailability is not reported as a data conflict
- [ ] Context-aware lock acquisition wherever a context exists
- [ ] The underlying error preserved unless the public contract deliberately replaces it
- [ ] A silent-error type used only when the command already printed the user-facing error
- [ ] Unreadable, malformed, or unresolved never turned into absent
- [ ] No success reported after skipping every requested target

## User-visible contract

- [ ] Every status has a distinct meaning
- [ ] Every success message follows a confirmed success
- [ ] Every warning names the affected path, remote, context, or agent when that helps
- [ ] Every remedy can fix the exact state that printed it
- [ ] The command does not print the same error twice
- [ ] Comments and docs name the actual recovery owner and execution path

## Test hygiene

- [ ] Focused test shown failing on the old code, then passing
- [ ] Entry through the production seam, not a nearby helper
- [ ] Outermost affected workflow result asserted, not only the helper's return value
- [ ] Assertion on the durable artifact or external result
- [ ] Aftermath checked with the next real operation that would expose leaked state
- [ ] Negative control proving unrelated behavior did not change
- [ ] Every backend that owns the same contract covered
- [ ] Native tooling or the real protocol used where it is the source of truth
- [ ] Real lock held, or the real competing operation run, for concurrency claims
- [ ] Related log fields asserted on the same record
- [ ] Raw serialized bytes asserted when encoding shape is part of the contract
- [ ] Parallel by default, except where the test mutates process-global state
- [ ] Isolated temporary repository, config directory, cache, and token storage
- [ ] No spawned binary inherits an interactive terminal

## Language-level choices that encode semantics (Go)

- Keep `ctx` bound to the caller context; name a derived timeout for its purpose
  (`discoveryCtx`), never shadow the caller's.
- Distinguish `os.ErrNotExist` from permission and I/O errors.
- Keep atomic writes, containment validation, and symlink policy together -- atomic replacement
  alone does not define safe ownership.
- Preserve file modes and unknown fields when editing user-owned configuration.
- Create a happens-before edge with a channel, mutex, or atomic in race-tested code.
- Treat `exec.Cmd.Wait` as a process result, not proof that a child protocol committed its operation.
- Inspect `exec.Cmd.Cancel` before using the default kill behavior for a stateful child protocol.
- Record local cancellation state when a cooperative child abort can still exit successfully.
- Close resources at the right lifetime boundary; a cleanup that deletes state is not the same
  operation as terminating a process.
- Check the module's language version before accepting syntax advice.

# Edge-case matrix

Walk the categories the change touches. These are ordinary states, not exotic ones -- every row
below appeared as a real review finding or a real bug.

## Git and paths

- [ ] Normal checkout
- [ ] Conventional linked worktree
- [ ] `.bare/worktrees` layout
- [ ] Separate Git directory
- [ ] Ordinary submodule
- [ ] Linked submodule
- [ ] Symlinked checkout or directory
- [ ] Symlinked final file, and dangling symlink
- [ ] Missing, unreadable, malformed, and non-regular paths
- [ ] Path containment still holds *after* symlink resolution
- [ ] No remote, fork remote, raw URL, multiple push URLs, elected remote

## State and persistence

- [ ] Absent
- [ ] User-owned but not managed by this tool
- [ ] Partial
- [ ] Current
- [ ] Outdated
- [ ] Invalid
- [ ] Unreadable
- [ ] Unresolved
- [ ] Unsupported
- [ ] Older persisted format
- [ ] Unknown fields preserved on rewrite
- [ ] Nil versus empty serialized values (`null` versus `[]`)

## Process and concurrency

- [ ] Cancellation before the durable write
- [ ] Cancellation during each state that holds an external resource or prepared transaction
- [ ] Cancellation after the write but before state save
- [ ] Graceful abort releases locks, temporary files, pipes, goroutines, and child processes
- [ ] The next real operation succeeds immediately after cancellation or failure
- [ ] Lock contention and lock timeout
- [ ] Safety, liveness, and fairness evaluated separately
- [ ] Deadline-bearing, cancelable-without-deadline, and non-cancelable callers retain their contract
- [ ] Shared blocking, polling, or retry changes audited across all caller classes
- [ ] Concurrent writer from another process (the real one, not an in-process stand-in)
- [ ] Cleanup that removes state a later step needs
- [ ] Retry after a partial operation
- [ ] Idempotent rerun

## Environment and user interaction

- [ ] Variable unset
- [ ] Variable present but empty
- [ ] Tool-specific inherited variables cannot override the explicitly selected target
- [ ] Ambient variables poisoned in tests to prove repository, config, and credential isolation
- [ ] No TTY
- [ ] Raw-mode TTY
- [ ] `NO_COLOR` or non-styled output
- [ ] Windows and missing POSIX shell
- [ ] Expired, missing, and explicitly selected login contexts

## Failure semantics

- [ ] Typed sentinel errors matched with `errors.Is`, never by string
- [ ] Presence distinguished from a non-empty value (`os.LookupEnv`)
- [ ] Caller cancellation propagated separately from a child timeout
- [ ] Process exit success distinguished from domain-operation success
- [ ] Protocol response, process result, and local cancellation state agree
- [ ] Internal timeout or contention traced to the outermost command, hook, request, or job result
- [ ] Contention or temporary unavailability is not reported as a data conflict
- [ ] Context-aware lock acquisition wherever a context exists
- [ ] The underlying error preserved unless the public contract deliberately replaces it
- [ ] A silent-error type used only when the command already printed the user-facing error
- [ ] Unreadable, malformed, or unresolved never turned into absent
- [ ] No success reported after skipping every requested target

## User-visible contract

- [ ] Every status has a distinct meaning
- [ ] Every success message follows a confirmed success
- [ ] Every warning names the affected path, remote, context, or agent when that helps
- [ ] Every remedy can fix the exact state that printed it
- [ ] The command does not print the same error twice
- [ ] Comments and docs name the actual recovery owner and execution path

## Test hygiene

- [ ] Focused test shown failing on the old code, then passing
- [ ] Entry through the production seam, not a nearby helper
- [ ] Outermost affected workflow result asserted, not only the helper's return value
- [ ] Assertion on the durable artifact or external result
- [ ] Aftermath checked with the next real operation that would expose leaked state
- [ ] Negative control proving unrelated behavior did not change
- [ ] Every backend that owns the same contract covered
- [ ] Native tooling or the real protocol used where it is the source of truth
- [ ] Real lock held, or the real competing operation run, for concurrency claims
- [ ] Related log fields asserted on the same record
- [ ] Raw serialized bytes asserted when encoding shape is part of the contract
- [ ] Parallel by default, except where the test mutates process-global state
- [ ] Isolated temporary repository, config directory, cache, and token storage
- [ ] No spawned binary inherits an interactive terminal

## Language-level choices that encode semantics (Go)

- Keep `ctx` bound to the caller context; name a derived timeout for its purpose
  (`discoveryCtx`), never shadow the caller's.
- Distinguish `os.ErrNotExist` from permission and I/O errors.
- Keep atomic writes, containment validation, and symlink policy together -- atomic replacement
  alone does not define safe ownership.
- Preserve file modes and unknown fields when editing user-owned configuration.
- Create a happens-before edge with a channel, mutex, or atomic in race-tested code.
- Treat `exec.Cmd.Wait` as a process result, not proof that a child protocol committed its operation.
- Inspect `exec.Cmd.Cancel` before using the default kill behavior for a stateful child protocol.
- Record local cancellation state when a cooperative child abort can still exit successfully.
- Close resources at the right lifetime boundary; a cleanup that deletes state is not the same
  operation as terminating a process.
- Check the module's language version before accepting syntax advice.

The consolidation remained necessary. Codex and status still parsed physical metadata; settings, review, investigation, trail, and setup still used the shared session/gitdir resolver/cache. Keeping these paths would preserve duplicate behavior and make the all-or-error resolver contract ineffective at real callers.

1. The live API was `gitdir.Open`, not `OpenForCurrentWorktree`. The rooted entry point is now named `OpenForCurrentWorktree`; `OpenAt`, `OpenPathIn`, `Reset`, and the shared `os.Root` lifetime remain intact.

## Hook capture and discovery tools

The shared bare-layout `.codex/hooks.json` was byte-identical to this worktree's snapshot. The live `worktree_path_not_discovered` diagnostic means the shared-root hooks are active; source inspection confirmed it is informational, not an inactive-hooks state. No copy, enabling, or trust-policy change was needed. The integration commit recorded checkpoint `01M1XWGPBS0FXGT9HHPB61DH0C`, confirming capture in this session.

Entire Graph v0.4.0 was used for discovery. Its working-tree search reported degraded coverage, so exact repository searches supplemented it. `/go:discover-related` was unavailable. `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` remains the sole physical traversal owner; its implementation and repository-open fallback rules are unchanged. It receives an explicit root and returns complete lexical metadata or an error. CWD discovery/cache remains in `paths.WorktreeRoot`.

Durable writes remain with the existing session, checkpoint, settings, review, and investigation stores. Canonical resolution precedes writes; their rooted I/O, atomic writes and locks remain the mutation owners. Metadata errors do not open a weaker storage path. No lock acquisition/release or checkpoint cancellation protocol was redesigned.

The final guard has no migration ledger. It retains four exact `.git` policy-inspection exceptions and eight exact flag/site semantic-query exceptions. Stale exceptions fail. Temporary independent `.git` reads, metadata queries behind constants, and stale exception entries each caused the actual ownership test to fail, and restoring the source made it pass.

Failure-policy proof warms real callers, damages `commondir`, and repairs it without cache clearing:

- required clone-preference reads/writes, review marker writes, review manifest reads/writes, investigation construction, trail scope paths, and cleanup preview fail;
- optional status branch lookup and explain filtering return no value;
- explicit-root settings load skips its unresolved preferences layer;
- Codex reports unresolved discovery;
- optional trail refresh still spawns when throttle metadata cannot resolve;
- repair recovers the prior preference and review content and permits subsequent operations.

The failure test was run through a temporary Go overlay against the original status implementation. It failed because old status still returned `linked` for damaged common-directory metadata; it passes with the migration.

## Layout and storage proof

The cross-consumer test uses real Git fixtures for ordinary, linked, `.bare`-backed, arbitrarily named bare storage, separate Git directory, ordinary submodule, linked submodule, submodule in a linked superproject, relative pointer, moved registration, and symlink alias layouts. It asserts exact IDs and `os.SameFile` agreement, then exercises actual session save/load, checkpoint enqueue/read, preferences, review markers, investigation findings/manifests, trail paths, Codex, status, and explain.

Existing canonical-owner tests supply malformed/missing/unreadable metadata, strict pointers, no bare fallback on damaged metadata, and physical identity cases. Existing Codex tests cover trust, backlinks, submodules, bare storage, installation, and cross-checkout writes. Existing settings tests cover no-follow safety. Existing strategy tests cover alias-independent lock ordering, real contention/release, cancellation/failure, and no-follow session storage. These focused suites passed on the integrated migration.

A new gitdir lifetime test verifies one shared handle across opens, confinement, failure after warm metadata, repair without closing shared handles, and explicit Reset closing/reopening the handle while preserving the stored file.

## Complete-operation Trace2 measurements

Compared the integrated prerequisite baseline to this migration using the same isolated fixture and test. Each operation starts with cleared CWD discovery and rooted-handle state. Counts include every real Git Trace2 start event inside the named entry point; fixture setup and positive control are outside the count. Every operation has a real Git positive control and a final asserted count.

| Complete entry point | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session constructor, cold CWD | 1 | 1 |
| Session constructor, explicit root | 0 | 0 |
| Push queue from an open repository | 0 | 0 |
| PrepareCommitMsg, no session | 2 | 2 |
| runStatus, enabled text status, no session | 5 | 4 |
| Codex ResolveHookDiscovery, cold CWD | 1 | 1 |

Prepare-commit retains its semantic repository-identity query. These are operation-entry-point counts, not full binary/Cobra startup measurements; they do not establish latency gains.

Physical Go source lines, including comments and blanks, in changed production files. Tests and benchmark/integration/test support are excluded. No new production file was added.

| File | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

The live `worktree_path_not_discovered` diagnostic means the shared-root hooks are active; source inspection confirmed it is informational, not an inactive-hooks state. No copy, enabling, or trust-policy change was needed. The integration commit recorded checkpoint `01M1XWGPBS0FXGT9HHPB61DH0C`, confirming capture in this session.

Entire Graph v0.4.0 was used for discovery. Its working-tree search reported degraded coverage, so exact repository searches supplemented it. `/go:discover-related` was unavailable. The planning notes and prerequisite PR bodies were treated as historical evidence, not live status. Checkpoint `01M1XAFRN8M65DVP35TSDCQMSM` metadata was inspected; its historical test claims were not substituted for current tests.

## Ownership and failure review

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` remains the sole physical traversal owner; its implementation and repository-open fallback rules are unchanged. It receives an explicit root and returns complete lexical metadata or an error. CWD discovery/cache remains in `paths.WorktreeRoot`.

Durable writes remain with the existing session, checkpoint, settings, review, and investigation stores. Canonical resolution precedes writes; their rooted I/O, atomic writes and locks remain the mutation owners. Metadata errors do not open a weaker storage path. No lock acquisition/release or checkpoint cancellation protocol was redesigned.

The final guard has no migration ledger. It retains four exact `.git` policy-inspection exceptions and eight exact flag/site semantic-query exceptions. Stale exceptions fail. Temporary independent `.git` reads, metadata queries behind constants, and stale exception entries each caused the actual ownership test to fail, and restoring the source made it pass.

Failure-policy proof warms real callers, damages `commondir`, and repairs it without cache clearing:

- required clone-preference reads/writes, review marker writes, review manifest reads/writes, investigation construction, trail scope paths, and cleanup preview fail;
- optional status branch lookup and explain filtering return no value;
- explicit-root settings load skips its unresolved preferences layer;
- Codex reports unresolved discovery;
- optional trail refresh still spawns when throttle metadata cannot resolve;
- repair recovers the prior preference and review content and permits subsequent operations.

The failure test was run through a temporary Go overlay against the original status implementation. It failed because old status still returned `linked` for damaged common-directory metadata; it passes with the migration.

The cross-consumer test uses real Git fixtures for ordinary, linked, `.bare`-backed, arbitrarily named bare storage, separate Git directory, ordinary submodule, linked submodule, submodule in a linked superproject, relative pointer, moved registration, and symlink alias layouts. It asserts exact IDs and `os.SameFile` agreement, then exercises actual session save/load, checkpoint enqueue/read, preferences, review markers, investigation findings/manifests, trail paths, Codex, status, and explain.

Existing canonical-owner tests supply malformed/missing/unreadable metadata, strict pointers, no bare fallback on damaged metadata, and physical identity cases. Existing Codex tests cover trust, backlinks, submodules, bare storage, installation, and cross-checkout writes. Existing settings tests cover no-follow safety. Existing strategy tests cover alias-independent lock ordering, real contention/release, cancellation/failure, and no-follow session storage. These focused suites passed on the integrated migration.

A new gitdir lifetime test verifies one shared handle across opens, confinement, failure after warm metadata, repair without closing shared handles, and explicit Reset closing/reopening the handle while preserving the stored file.

Start with an extensive independent review. You own that review: treat this handoff as starting evidence, assess whether the task is still needed and correctly scoped, identify stale assumptions or a smaller/better approach, then proceed with scoped implementation if the review supports it.

Its `GIT_METADATA_TRAVERSAL_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` and `GIT_METADATA_TRAVERSAL_THERMO_NUCLEAR_REVIEW.md` provide historical design evidence. First, establish a safe current base:
1. Read current repository/agent instructions and inspect local changes before altering the destination branch. Re-check live PR heads, reviews, CI, and main; the local prerequisite heads already differ from GitHub.
2. Fetch current main and prerequisite branch tips. If splits 3 and 4 have merged, refresh the clean split-5 branch onto main. Otherwise integrate their current implementations locally in dependency order, preserving any newer fixes. Do not blindly cherry-pick the old hashes above or port the original monolithic PR wholesale.
3. Split 5 requires all four prerequisite implementations present before deleting their shared APIs. Local integration is allowed; publishing split 5 against main waits for prerequisite landing and a narrow refreshed diff.
4. The split plan records a shared bare-layout Codex hook snapshot: the shared root `.codex/hooks.json` should be refreshed from the chosen worktree before its session starts. Inspect the current documented hook setup and use the supported mechanism; preserve ownership/trust policy and do not blindly copy or enable hooks. If this bootstrap was not done before launch, assess it before relying on checkpoint capture.

Remaining implementation:
- Migrate physical metadata traversal in Codex discovery, settings clone preferences, status, review, investigate, trail, setup/cleanup, explain, dispatch, benchmarks, and integration fixtures. Re-inventory current callers rather than treating this list as exhaustive.
- Delete `paths.GetWorktreeID`, its marker parser and obsolete tests, the legacy exported `gitrepo.ResolveDotGitPath` / `ResolveCommonGitPath` composition surface, forwarding wrappers, stale cache-reset calls, and cache-only tests once the last callers migrate.
- Explicitly include the deferred session/gitdir cleanup. Split 3's live PR says `session.GetGitCommonDir`, the clearing API, and the `gitdir` common-directory resolver/cache remain for outside consumers. The original split plan expected earlier deletion, but that did not happen in split 3. Remove `gitdir.CommonDir`, `CommonDirForWorktree`, `ClearCache`, and subprocess/cache state only after validating their current call graph. Preserve `gitdir.OpenForCurrentWorktree`, `OpenAt`, `OpenPathIn`, and `Reset`, including rooted-handle lifetime.

Split 4 deliberately allows retired ledger query entries to become diagnostics during migration; the final guard must no longer depend on that transition behavior.
- Add final cross-consumer agreement, failure-policy, identity/layout, and complete-operation Trace2 proof. Record production line-count and subprocess-count changes.

Contracts to preserve:
- `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata(root)` remains the sole physical traversal owner: explicit non-empty root, cleaned absolute lexical paths, complete metadata or an error; no subprocess, context, options, layout enum, or cache.
- `paths.WorktreeRoot` retains CWD discovery and its existing cache. Rooted/no-follow storage and locking must remain intact. A bare store is not a worktree; repository opening must not downgrade malformed/unreadable metadata into a weaker fallback.
- Preserve required failures and optional warning/skip/fail-open behavior at each consumer. Preserve Codex trust, backlink, submodule/bare handling, diagnostics, installation, and cross-checkout-write policy. Preserve settings safety and caller-visible lexical status/trail paths.

Output and boundaries:

- Keep comments short and limited to non-obvious invariants/contracts; no agent/process/task labels in production comments.
- Keep progress/handoff notes local. Do not push, merge, create/close PRs or issues, label, or post public comments without explicit authorization. Landing order remains split 3, split 4, then split 5; tracking-PR closeout comes after all replacements land.

# Edge-case matrix

Walk the categories the change touches. These are ordinary states, not exotic ones -- every row
below appeared as a real review finding or a real bug.

## Git and paths

- [ ] Normal checkout
- [ ] Conventional linked worktree
- [ ] `.bare/worktrees` layout
- [ ] Separate Git directory
- [ ] Ordinary submodule
- [ ] Linked submodule
- [ ] Symlinked checkout or directory
- [ ] Symlinked final file, and dangling symlink
- [ ] Missing, unreadable, malformed, and non-regular paths
- [ ] Path containment still holds *after* symlink resolution
- [ ] No remote, fork remote, raw URL, multiple push URLs, elected remote

## State and persistence

- [ ] Absent
- [ ] User-owned but not managed by this tool
- [ ] Partial
- [ ] Current
- [ ] Outdated
- [ ] Invalid
- [ ] Unreadable
- [ ] Unresolved
- [ ] Unsupported
- [ ] Older persisted format
- [ ] Unknown fields preserved on rewrite
- [ ] Nil versus empty serialized values (`null` versus `[]`)

## Process and concurrency

- [ ] Cancellation before the durable write
- [ ] Cancellation during each state that holds an external resource or prepared transaction
- [ ] Cancellation after the write but before state save
- [ ] Graceful abort releases locks, temporary files, pipes, goroutines, and child processes
- [ ] The next real operation succeeds immediately after cancellation or failure
- [ ] Lock contention and lock timeout
- [ ] Safety, liveness, and fairness evaluated separately
- [ ] Deadline-bearing, cancelable-without-deadline, and non-cancelable callers retain their contract
- [ ] Shared blocking, polling, or retry changes audited across all caller classes
- [ ] Concurrent writer from another process (the real one, not an in-process stand-in)
- [ ] Cleanup that removes state a later step needs
- [ ] Retry after a partial operation
- [ ] Idempotent rerun

## Environment and user interaction

- [ ] Variable unset
- [ ] Variable present but empty
- [ ] Tool-specific inherited variables cannot override the explicitly selected target
- [ ] Ambient variables poisoned in tests to prove repository, config, and credential isolation
- [ ] No TTY
- [ ] Raw-mode TTY
- [ ] `NO_COLOR` or non-styled output
- [ ] Windows and missing POSIX shell
- [ ] Expired, missing, and explicitly selected login contexts

## Failure semantics

- [ ] Typed sentinel errors matched with `errors.Is`, never by string
- [ ] Presence distinguished from a non-empty value (`os.LookupEnv`)
- [ ] Caller cancellation propagated separately from a child timeout
- [ ] Process exit success distinguished from domain-operation success
- [ ] Protocol response, process result, and local cancellation state agree
- [ ] Internal timeout or contention traced to the outermost command, hook, request, or job result
- [ ] Contention or temporary unavailability is not reported as a data conflict
- [ ] Context-aware lock acquisition wherever a context exists
- [ ] The underlying error preserved unless the public contract deliberately replaces it
- [ ] A silent-error type used only when the command already printed the user-facing error
- [ ] Unreadable, malformed, or unresolved never turned into absent
- [ ] No success reported after skipping every requested target

## User-visible contract

- [ ] Every status has a distinct meaning
- [ ] Every success message follows a confirmed success
- [ ] Every warning names the affected path, remote, context, or agent when that helps
- [ ] Every remedy can fix the exact state that printed it
- [ ] The command does not print the same error twice
- [ ] Comments and docs name the actual recovery owner and execution path

## Test hygiene

- [ ] Focused test shown failing on the old code, then passing
- [ ] Entry through the production seam, not a nearby helper
- [ ] Outermost affected workflow result asserted, not only the helper's return value
- [ ] Assertion on the durable artifact or external result
- [ ] Aftermath checked with the next real operation that would expose leaked state
- [ ] Negative control proving unrelated behavior did not change
- [ ] Every backend that owns the same contract covered
- [ ] Native tooling or the real protocol used where it is the source of truth
- [ ] Real lock held, or the real competing operation run, for concurrency claims
- [ ] Related log fields asserted on the same record
- [ ] Raw serialized bytes asserted when encoding shape is part of the contract
- [ ] Parallel by default, except where the test mutates process-global state
- [ ] Isolated temporary repository, config directory, cache, and token storage
- [ ] No spawned binary inherits an interactive terminal

## Language-level choices that encode semantics (Go)

- Keep `ctx` bound to the caller context; name a derived timeout for its purpose
  (`discoveryCtx`), never shadow the caller's.
- Distinguish `os.ErrNotExist` from permission and I/O errors.
- Keep atomic writes, containment validation, and symlink policy together -- atomic replacement
  alone does not define safe ownership.
- Preserve file modes and unknown fields when editing user-owned configuration.
- Create a happens-before edge with a channel, mutex, or atomic in race-tested code.
- Treat `exec.Cmd.Wait` as a process result, not proof that a child protocol committed its operation.
- Inspect `exec.Cmd.Cancel` before using the default kill behavior for a stateful child protocol.
- Record local cancellation state when a cooperative child abort can still exit successfully.
- Close resources at the right lifetime boundary; a cleanup that deletes state is not the same
  operation as terminating a process.
- Check the module's language version before accepting syntax advice.

text='''# Split 5 independent review and verification

Local review record, 2026-09-07. Do not commit this directory.

## Dependency/base findings

- The prepared destination was clean at `ee6d53f3d3398267358e8f9d306267c87a088101`; it did not contain the prerequisite implementations.
- Live upstream main fetched at `3d1b73ff2a669a0df7afaca24f4c8d0cca1435e7`.

- Split 4, PR #2305, remains OPEN / REVIEW_REQUIRED at `1c7280a4793fedf3da46acb3af5b0dd1ab8dcfb9`.

- Integration baseline `mise run check` passed in 349.47s, including deterministic canaries. No paid agent calls.
- Tracking PR #2190 remains open. No remote modifications were made. Publication waits for split 3, then split 4, and a refreshed narrow diff against main.

## Independent scope assessment

The consolidation remained necessary. Codex and status still parsed physical metadata; settings, review, investigation, trail, and setup still used the shared session/gitdir resolver/cache. Keeping these paths would preserve duplicate behavior and make the all-or-error resolver contract ineffective at real callers.

Corrections to the handoff/old plan:

1. The live API was `gitdir.Open`, not `OpenForCurrentWorktree`. The rooted entry point is now named `OpenForCurrentWorktree`; `OpenAt`, `OpenPathIn`, `Reset`, and the shared `os.Root` lifetime remain intact.
2. Split 3 deferred session forwarding/cache deletion. This split removes those APIs only after migrating their remaining callers.
3. Dispatch's existing candidate filters and root discovery are semantic/policy duties. No dispatch rewrite was necessary. Adoption, strategy ownership, and trail reuse retain individually justified Git validation queries.
4. Current status does not print worktree paths in its active-session section. The proof checks preservation of stored lexical paths and branch lookup through aliases. Trail's exact printed path is tested directly.
5. The optional `hookperf` fixture was already stale: it used the removed `agent.AgentType` alias and `FirstPrompt`. Its already-touched fixture now uses `types.AgentType` and `LastPrompt`; only compilation was run, not its network-backed benchmarks.
6. The separate GIT_COMMON_DIR environment-scrubbing fix is still uncommitted in its own worktree. This branch does not include it. Trail's explicitly targeted semantic probes use the existing environment helper and inherit that helper's known limitation.

## Hook capture and discovery tools

The shared bare-layout `.codex/hooks.json` was byte-identical to this worktree's snapshot. The live `worktree_path_not_discovered` diagnostic means the shared-root hooks are active; source inspection confirmed it is informational, not an inactive-hooks state. No copy, enabling, or trust-policy change was needed. The integration commit recorded checkpoint `01M1XWGPBS0FXGT9HHPB61DH0C`, confirming capture in this session.

Entire Graph v0.4.0 was used for discovery. Its working-tree search reported degraded coverage, so exact repository searches supplemented it. `/go:discover-related` was unavailable. The planning notes and prerequisite PR bodies were treated as historical evidence, not live status. Checkpoint `01M1XAFRN8M65DVP35TSDCQMSM` metadata was inspected; its historical test claims were not substituted for current tests.

## Ownership and failure review

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` remains the sole physical traversal owner; its implementation and repository-open fallback rules are unchanged. It receives an explicit root and returns complete lexical metadata or an error. CWD discovery/cache remains in `paths.WorktreeRoot`.

Durable writes remain with the existing session, checkpoint, settings, review, and investigation stores. Canonical resolution precedes writes; their rooted I/O, atomic writes and locks remain the mutation owners. Metadata errors do not open a weaker storage path. No lock acquisition/release or checkpoint cancellation protocol was redesigned.

The final guard has no migration ledger. It retains four exact `.git` policy-inspection exceptions and eight exact flag/site semantic-query exceptions. Stale exceptions fail. Temporary independent `.git` reads, metadata queries behind constants, and stale exception entries each caused the actual ownership test to fail, and restoring the source made it pass.

Failure-policy proof warms real callers, damages `commondir`, and repairs it without cache clearing:

- required clone-preference reads/writes, review marker writes, review manifest reads/writes, investigation construction, trail scope paths, and cleanup preview fail;
- optional status branch lookup and explain filtering return no value;
- explicit-root settings load skips its unresolved preferences layer;
- Codex reports unresolved discovery;
- optional trail refresh still spawns when throttle metadata cannot resolve;
- repair recovers the prior preference and review content and permits subsequent operations.

The failure test was run through a temporary Go overlay against the original status implementation. It failed because old status still returned `linked` for damaged common-directory metadata; it passes with the migration.

## Layout and storage proof

The cross-consumer test uses real Git fixtures for ordinary, linked, `.bare`-backed, arbitrarily named bare storage, separate Git directory, ordinary submodule, linked submodule, submodule in a linked superproject, relative pointer, moved registration, and symlink alias layouts. Existing canonical-owner tests supply malformed/missing/unreadable metadata, strict pointers, no bare fallback on damaged metadata, and physical identity cases. Existing Codex tests cover trust, backlinks, submodules, bare storage, installation, and cross-checkout writes. Existing settings tests cover no-follow safety. Existing strategy tests cover alias-independent lock ordering, real contention/release, cancellation/failure, and no-follow session storage. These focused suites passed on the integrated migration.

A new gitdir lifetime test verifies one shared handle across opens, confinement, failure after warm metadata, repair without closing shared handles, and explicit Reset closing/reopening the handle while preserving the stored file.

## Complete-operation Trace2 measurements

Compared the integrated prerequisite baseline to this migration using the same isolated fixture and test. Each operation starts with cleared CWD discovery and rooted-handle state. Counts include every real Git Trace2 start event inside the named entry point; fixture setup and positive control are outside the count. Every operation has a real Git positive control and a final asserted count.

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

# Entire - CLI

This repo contains the CLI for Entire.

## Architecture

- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh

## Key Directories

### Commands (`cmd/`)

- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (ephemeral and persistent)
- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))

### Command Layout

The visible CLI is organized around a set of noun groups plus a small set of
top-level verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb. Newer
experimental command families are discoverable through `entire labs` and
their canonical paths are always runnable.

Experimental commands are gated by a build-time visibility flag (the
`cmd/entire/cli/experimental` package): they are shown — grouped under an
"Experimental commands:" help section — in developer and nightly builds, and
hidden in stable release builds. Visibility is toggled by `experimental.Visible`
(default `"true"`), which GoReleaser stamps `"false"` only on stable tags
(`.Prerelease` empty); nightly (`vX.Y.Z-nightly.*`) and local builds leave it at
the default. Register a command as experimental with `experimental.Register(parent,
child)` instead of `parent.AddCommand(child)`. Gating only controls visibility —
the commands are always runnable in every build.

- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `tokens`, `stop`, `attach`, `adopt`, `resume`, `current`.
  `resume` with a branch arg switches to it and resumes its session; with no arg
  it opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions (across all worktrees),
  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
  `adopt` moves an active session from another repo or worktree into the current
  worktree and resets target-local checkpoint bookkeeping so future commits link
  to the adopted session from the new location.
- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`.
  `explain` also takes `--repo <owner/name>`, the drill-down for a cross-repo
  `search` hit: it reads the checkpoint from that repo's entire-api cell over
  HTTP (`/repos/{repo_id}/checkpoints/{id}` plus `.../transcript/raw`) rather
  than fetching git objects, so a foreign checkpoint never enters this repo's
  object store, ref namespace, or `tokens profile`. It needs a full checkpoint
  ID and a pushed checkpoint; `--commit`, `--session`, `--search-all`, and
  `--generate` are rejected with it, and naming the current repo is a no-op
  that falls through to the local path. See `checkpoint_api_reader.go`
  (`apiCheckpointReader`, which implements the two checkpoint reader tiers and
  deliberately not `Writer`) and `explain_repo.go`.
- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`, plus
  `token` (prints the active control-plane bearer to stdout for scripting/curl;
  honors `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, else the refreshed active-context login JWT). `token`
  also takes `--jurisdiction <slug>` (e.g. `us`, `eu`), which instead mints a
  jurisdictional identity token (RFC 8693 exchange, `scope=openid`,
  `aud=<jurisdiction host>`) for that jurisdiction's entire-api cells (e.g.
  `https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io/api/v1`), which reject the control-plane
  bearer; it exchanges `ENTIRE_TOKEN` when set (deriving the environment from the
  env token's `aud`), else the active login. `auth status` shows the caller's
  home jurisdiction so the slug is discoverable. `logout`
  takes `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
- `org`: control-plane organization management — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`
- `project`: control-plane project management — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`
- `repo`: control-plane repository lifecycle — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`,
  `clone`, plus the `mirror` and `visibility` subtrees. Git content operations
  (log, diff, …) are intentionally out of scope. The `mirror` subtree is
  server-side (`create`, `list`, `get`, `remove`, `collaborators`) with one
  exception: `mirror use` repoints the *current clone's* git remote at a mirror
  (local git config only — it creates nothing server-side). Interactively it
  picks among the repo's placements and asks whether to replace the remote
  (preserving the old URL under `--upstream`) or add a separate one;
  non-interactively it repoints `--remote` directly. Both `use` and `clone`
  choose a placement through the shared `selectPlacement` picker. `clone`
  accepts a native `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref (or the `<project>/<repo>`
  shorthand — the `gh`/`et` forge tokens can never be project names, which are
  3+ chars server-side, so the grammar is unambiguous; both segments must also
  match the server's name charsets, so `git@github.com:foo/bar` is not a
  shorthand), a mirror `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` ref, or a full `entire://` URL
  passed through verbatim. A ref matching none of these gets a targeted error
  (`invalidCloneRefError`): a GitHub URL is pointed at its `/gh/` form, a
  malformed `gh/` ref keeps the mirror parser's reason, anything else lists
  the accepted shapes.
  A native ref resolves project → repo ULID → `GetRepo`, whose response is the
  only one carrying both `clusterHost` and `path`, and clones
  `entire://<clusterHost><path>` from the repo's home cluster (no `.git`
  suffix — the server strips it for `/gh/` paths only; `--cluster` is
  rejected on native refs).
- `grant`: manage access grants and org membership — `org`, `project`, and `repo`
  each support `add` / `list` / `remove`

Experimental commands (gated by the build-time visibility flag above — visible
and grouped under "Experimental commands:" in developer/nightly builds, hidden
in stable releases, always runnable): `tokens`, `import`, `review`,
`investigate`, `blame`, `why`, `experts`, `runner`, and `checkpoint policy`.
`tokens` is also advertised through `entire labs`.

Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
`configure`, `agent-help`, `api`, `search`. `search` is the canonical
spelling (visible in every build, grouped with Sessions & Checkpoints);
`checkpoint search` stays a working alias of the same command.

`api` is an authenticated passthrough to Entire's HTTP APIs (gh-style): it
attaches the right bearer and dials the right host so callers don't plumb auth
themselves. `--to core` (default) hits the control plane; `--to cell` hits an
entire-api cell. `--jurisdiction <slug>` (e.g. `us`, `eu`) targets a specific
jurisdiction's cell instead of the caller's home cell and implies `--to cell`
(cell routing + identity-token exchange live in `auth.NewEntireAPICellClient`
via `auth.CellTarget`). `{owner}`/`{repo}`/`{repo_id}` in the path are filled
from the current repo's origin remote. It is an escape hatch, so it is absent
from `agent-help`'s curated listing but stays in `entire help` and agent-help's
footer — an agent that needs raw access must find it rather than hand-roll curl
with a token.

`agent-help` renders machine-readable, agent-facing usage live from the Cobra
command tree (so it always matches the installed binary): bare prints a curated
"when to use entire" map; `agent-help <command>` drills into one command's
current flags; `--json` emits structured output. It is the single source of
truth the first-turn context injection and the `--agent-help-skill` skill point
agents at, instead of enumerating a surface that goes stale.

#### Where agent-facing text goes

| What you have | Where it goes |
| --- | --- |
| A new command | `agentHelpClassification` in `agent_help_cmd.go` — one entry, keyed by command path, carrying `audience` and `listed` |
| "When to use this at all" advice for agents | `agentHelpGuidance` — **never** cobra `Short`/`Long` |
| A fact humans need too (e.g. "this output is not stable") | cobra `Long`. Human help is a reference, not a lecture: whoever typed `--help` already chose the command |
| A per-task command recommendation | `agent-help`, which is pulled on demand. **Never** the first-turn injection, which carries only invariants true on every turn |

**Flag it; don't decide it.** Whether a command is `listed`, and whether it is
read-only / task-driven / user-owned, are product judgment calls — they change
what agents do unprompted in every user's repo. Take the safe default
(unlisted, user-owned), then say in the PR what you picked and why so a human
can move it. Never quietly promote a command into the listing or into
read-only.

CI enforces the mechanical parts, so trust these rather than re-deriving them:
every advertised top-level command and every child of a listed group is
classified; a read-only group contains no writing subcommand; guidance text
never appears in a command's `Short`/`Long`.

Hidden commands opt into being advertised here by setting
`Annotations[agentHelpAnnotation] = "true"` (e.g. `trail`). Because `agent-help`
renders live and lists non-hidden commands, the experimental commands appear in
`agent-help` in developer/nightly builds and are absent in stable releases — the
advertised surface is build-dependent, matching what `entire help` shows.
No-channel agents (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, MCP hosts — no
context-injection channel and no agent-help skill template) reach it without an
active push. All of them can discover it passively: it is visible in `entire
help`, the `entire status` footer points at it, and `entire status --json`
exposes it as the `agent_help` field. On top of that, Factory AI Droid (which is
banner-only) gets the pointer appended to its SessionStart hook banner, and
MCP-host agents can launch the hidden `entire mcp` stdio server, which exposes
`agent_help` and `entire_status` as MCP tools using the same live rendering.
Enabling a no-channel agent with `--agent-help-skill` reports the skill
unsupported and points the agent at this passive path instead.

Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
`checkpoint`.

Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`, `__sweep_sessions`, `mcp` (MCP
stdio server for MCP-host agents).

Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.
